titles: Why Rome Destroyed Carthage (Even After It Surrendered)
Carthage Gave Up Its Weapons. Rome Burned It Anyway.
The Fall of Carthage Explained in Maps
hook: Rome had already beaten Carthage. Carthage paid, obeyed, and even handed over its weapons. So why did Rome come back fifty years later and burn it to the ground? A fresh fig, a king who was almost ninety, one impossible order, and a myth about salt. Told with animated maps, modern borders, and the ancient sources on screen. Carthage stood next to today's Tunis, in Tunisia.

chapters.c0a: Why burn a city that already surrendered?

pinned_comment: Cato said Rome would only be safe once Carthage was gone. Scipio Nasica said Rome needed a rival to stay strong. Who was right?
